body:
Given the limitations of this approach, like long press not being handled and no gestures, I started looking into if this can be a plugin instead. As a plugin it can be more opinionated and have extra features useful for emulating touch or mouse events specifically.
Handling multiple windows is tricky, but it almost can do it. `DisplayServer` has a `window_set_input_event_callback` that lets you intercept all input events that go to a window, but the default handler for it `Window::_window_input` is not exposed, so you cannot return the input back to the default implementation.
There's a hack to send notification enter events to the window to reset it, but that causes errors and doesn't work if you want to intercept the event then have it continue.
I think it makes sense to expose `Window::_window_input`, since having the default implementation is useful when changing `window_set_input_event_callback` and its not possible to work around since it calls `Window::_input_from_window` which popups use and is unexposed.

DisplayServer also should have a way to reliably tell when new windows are opened, so it can be set for every window. But it can be worked around by polling the window list.

Using `window_set_input_event_callback` won't work with the regular emulate settings, but they aren't very complicated and can be implemented manually.

I'm going to open another PR to expose it.
